subject: Dedicated capacity follow-up: GPU preference, token volumes & target $/1M
messages:
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jacob Miller <jacob.miller@optihealth.com>, Sylvia Cho <sylvia.cho@optihealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 14 Aug 2026 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap + numbers we discussed (Dedicated capacity)

Thanks again for the call today — good discussion. Quick recap and the numbers we need to firm up so we can build a dedicated SKU that hits your latency and cost goals. Please confirm or correct any items below.

Key items from today:
- Workload: real-time assistant + structured responses for claims intake and triage; replacement for internal rule engine on ~60% of flows.
- Latency target: 95th < 150 ms for short prompts (avg 400 tokens); tail is important for UX.
- Expected steady-state volume: ~1.2 billion tokens / month (this is your internal estimate).
- Peak burst: up to 400 million tokens in a single day during heavy policy update windows.
- Average convo: ~550 tokens / response (including system prompt + user + assistant).
- Quality target: same or better than current tuned Llama-3 variant; open to 4-bit quantization with validation.

Pricing & budget guidance you shared:
- Target unit economics: looking for ~$12-$18 per 1M tokens for production traffic (goal to make dedicated comparable to hosted but with isolation).
- Budget band: $40k - $90k / month for reserved capacity (flexible depending on GPU choice and burst capacity).

Questions / asks for OptiHealth to confirm:
1) Can you confirm the 1.2B tokens/month is the conservative baseline (not peak)?
2) Do you have an internal SLA or availability requirement beyond latency (e.g., 99.9% uptime)?
3) Any hard constraint on GPU vendor/type (NVIDIA H100 vs A100 80GB) or preference for preemption-free instances?

Next steps from Redwood:
- We will produce a preliminary Dedicated SKU with two options: H100-heavy (lower latency, higher $) and A100-optimized (better $/token with aggressive quantization).
- Include both steady-state reserved sizing and a burst plan (short-term credit or on-demand fallback).
- Draft a 30/60/90-day mutual action plan and a rough quote (PDF) for procurement.

I'll draft the quote and send it to procurement and your team by EOD tomorrow. If anything above is off, please reply inline.

Best,

Laura Bennett
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com
+1 (415) 555-0124

Date: Fri, 14 Aug 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: OptiHealth discovery — need sizing + cost calc

Folks — forwarding the OptiHealth recap. They gave a 1.2B tokens/month baseline and big single-day peaks (~400M). Latency SLO: 95th < 150ms for ~400-token requests.

What I need from you for the draft:
- Ben: preliminary Dedicated SKU options (reserved capacity) with monthly price ranges for two configs:
  1) 4x H100 (or equivalent) reserved with burst to on-demand, target $/1M tokens and monthly commit
  2) 6x A100-80GB with 4-bit quantization profile — lower $/1M but needs validation on quality
- Priyom: any upfront discounting guidance vs hosted per-1M targets (they want $12-$18 / 1M).
- Evelyn/Rishi: confirmation on feasibility for latency SLO at those volumes (auto-batching + prefix cache) and any caveats for long-tail requests.

Assumptions to call out in the quote:
- 1.2B tokens/month steady (we should explicitly show how that maps to #tokens/sec avg and peak)
- 30% safety buffer for KV cache miss + cold-starts; show cost delta for adding 25% burst capacity reserve

I'll assemble the math in the quote doc and loop in procurement if they push for an annual commit. Aim: review internally by EOD so I can send a polished quote to OptiHealth tomorrow morning.

Thanks — laura

Laura Bennett
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

From: Jacob Miller <jacob.miller@optihealth.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Sylvia Cho <sylvia.cho@optihealth.com>
Cc: procurement@optihealth.com
Date: Sat, 15 Aug 2026 08:17:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + numbers we discussed (Dedicated capacity)

Thanks Laura — quick clarifications from our side after the team sync: 
- The 1.2B tokens/month is our best conservative estimate for month-to-month active users. It excludes heavy episodic loads.
- Peak day of 400M was our estimate during product launch weeks; that's an upper bound — typical peak days are ~180-220M.
- Latency: 95th < 150ms is negotiable, but anything above 200ms will degrade conversion on our intake flow. So please show an option that meets 150ms and a cheaper option that targets ~200ms.
- GPU constraint: we prefer non-preemptible hardware. No strict vendor lock, but our infra team favors H100 if the price delta vs A100 is < 25%.
- Contract horizon: we're targeting a 12-month reserved commit if the economics work; otherwise 6 months with a review.

One ask: can you show the per-1M token cost with and without aggressive quantization (i.e., 4-bit PTQ) and note any quality/regression risk? Procurement wants a simple per-1M line to compare with our hosted baseline.

Thanks — Jacob
